entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcin of Wrocimowice (d. 1441) emerged as a pivotal Polish knight and diplomat during the early 15th century, a period defined by the burgeoning power of the Jagiellonian dynasty and intense geopolitical rivalry with the Teutonic Order. Best known for his iconic role as the standard-bearer of the Kraków banner at the Battle of Grunwald in 1410, he symbolized the martial prowess and national spirit of the united Polish-Lithuanian forces. His career spanned significant military engagements and crucial diplomatic missions, underscoring his importance in shaping the nascent Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth's international standing.

His most celebrated moment occurred on July 15, 1410, when, as the custodian of the Grand Banner of the Kingdom of Poland, Marcin of Wrocimowice bravely defended the royal standard after it was momentarily knocked down during a fierce charge by the Teutonic Knights. This act of valor, often cited in Polish historical accounts, rallied the Polish forces and contributed to the decisive victory over the Teutonic Order, a turning point in Central European history. Beyond the battlefield, Marcin served as a royal envoy, participating in critical diplomatic endeavors, including representing the Polish crown at the Council of Constance (1414-1418), where he advocated for Polish interests and challenged the Teutonic Order's propaganda.

Marcin's contributions solidified the Jagiellonian dynasty's prestige and military might, paving the way for Poland's ascendancy as a major European power in the 15th century. His actions at Grunwald became a cornerstone of Polish national identity, invoked through centuries of struggle for independence and sovereignty. His diplomatic work at Constance, alongside figures like Paweł Włodkowic, helped establish legal precedents for state sovereignty and religious tolerance, influencing subsequent international relations and canon law.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Marcin of Wrocimowice's role as the standard-bearer at Grunwald was a powerful symbol of Polish military might, contributing to the decisive defeat of the Teutonic Order and solidifying the Jagiellonian dynasty's regional dominance. His diplomatic service further cemented Poland's standing in 15th-century European politics.
